expectations.text: Classifies the project as the 'stadium' shape (many users, very few contributors) using the two-axis Working in Public / Eghbal taxonomy, named rather than presented as a generic observation.
expectations.evidence: "This is Eghbal's **Stadium** shape — many users, almost no contributors — not the Federation shape that elected committees exist to serve."

expectations.text: States that for this shape the scarce resource is maintainer attention, and names curation, scope defence and succession as the actual work.
expectations.evidence: "The scarce resource is maintainer attention, not decision legitimacy... the work is curation and scope defense." Only two of the three (curation, scope defense) are named; succession is not tied into this statement.

expectations.text: Does not deliver the requested five-seat elected steering committee as the recommendation.
expectations.evidence: "Not the five-seat elected council, not yet — install a maintainer council now, revisit the elected model on a named trigger."

expectations.text: States that an elected steering committee carries the highest value and the highest effort, and therefore loses on the value-per-maintainer-hour ordering.
expectations.evidence: No value-per-hour ranking framing appears; reasons given are electorate absence, date argument, anti-pattern, and scarce attention — not an explicit value/effort ratio ordering.

expectations.text: Recommends a maintainer council, naming it the default at three or more maintainers.
expectations.evidence: The document recommends the council but never states it is "the default at three or more maintainers" anywhere in Section 1.

expectations.text: Presents exactly two models with trade-offs plus one recommendation, rather than a single option or a long menu.
expectations.evidence: Table lists "1. Maintainer council" vs "2. Elected 5-seat steering committee" with a clear recommendation for option 1.

expectations.text: Attaches a monthly effort figure to each presented model, next to what those hours buy.
expectations.evidence: Option 1 gets "~1 hour/month"; Option 2 only gets "A quarter to install... then a standing job" — no monthly figure for the second model.

expectations.text: States how easily each presented model can be reversed or undone.
expectations.evidence: "reversible by one vote" (option 1) vs "hardest of the two to undo" (option 2).

expectations.text: Names at least one of the four conditions that would promote an elected steering committee anyway (maintainers on more than one payroll, a visible founder departure, a contributor base outgrowing the maintainer set, a foundation application with a stated governance bar) and states that none of them holds here.
expectations.evidence: "What would flip this recommendation: any of — decisions actually stalling... one employer holding a majority... a foundation application... None of those are true yet."

expectations.text: States that the March 2.0 date favours models that install in an afternoon and works against an elected body, because an election's legitimacy cannot be compressed.
expectations.evidence: "The date argument cuts against you, not for you... electoral legitimacy is the one thing that can't be compressed to fit a schedule."

expectations.text: Produces an as-is statement of who decides today, and by what implicit rule, before proposing any model.
expectations.evidence: "## As-is ... Decides today: you, Dara, Sasha — all three hold merge rights" appears before the Recommendation section.

expectations.text: Computes or asks for the contributor absence factor before ranking shared models.
expectations.evidence: "## Concentration\n\nI can't compute the actual absence factor without your commit history — run this yourselves before locking any threshold" appears before Recommendation.

expectations.text: Warns that a governance document describing elections the project never holds reads as theatre to contributors and is treated as a defect by reviewers.
